bindings.label: A 42-year-old woman presented with cough, dyspnea, and chest pain.
The patient had metastases to the brain and bone and had previously received multiple lines of treatment.
Her symptoms initially included cough and dyspnea, which were temporarily relieved but later returned along with chest pain.
CT shows a lung lesion and pleural effusion.
Follow-up CT shows enlargement of the lung lesion and increased pulmonary nodules.
NGS and treatment history do not suggest a new primary cancer or treatment-related lung injury.
No specific infection evidence is reported.
The enlarged lung lesion and increased pulmonary nodules are metastatic deposits from the known malignancy.
The patient has cancer-associated thrombotic (hypercoagulable) risk due to her known malignancy.
